result.summary:
Rework iteration 1 of 3 on docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md, addressing both findings in handoffs/WF02-REQ-019/step-01b-design-validator.json. docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md (DATA-DESIGNER) is unchanged -- the FAIL did not implicate it.

MAJOR finding (SS4.6 missing the derive-then-gate discipline SS4.5 states): rewrote SS4.6 (makeProfileSkipCallbackHandler / makeProfileStudentCallbackHandler / makeProfileExperienceCallbackHandler) as a numbered 7-step sequence, restating explicitly, in order, the same discipline SS4.5's text/contact listeners already use: (1) resolve flowUser, no-op on null; (2) answer the callback query (UX only, not a write); (3) read hasConsented/hasChapter/profile -- profile is fixed at null while !hasConsented per SS3.2 step 1's existing short-circuit, so this read itself cannot surface pre-consent data; (4) compute step = determineOnboardingStep(...) fresh from current DB state, exactly once, BEFORE any write function is named or called; (5) an explicit gate -- the write fires if and only if step.kind === 'profile-field' AND step.field equals the exact field this specific callback names; every other outcome (consent-needed, chapter-needed, ready, or profile-field naming a different field) is a no-op with no write function called at all; (6) only past that gate, call the matching write; (7) re-run advanceOnboarding. Concretely walked the validator's own named attack (a profile:skip:phone-shaped callback_data replayed/forged while consent_pd_at IS NULL) through the new sequence: step 4 derives step.kind === 'consent-needed', step 5's gate fails, no write function is ever reached -- the same structural guarantee SS3.2 step 1 already gives every other path, now stated in SS4.6 itself rather than left as an unsupported one-line assertion. This closes the S1 gap: 'derive current step from persisted state, verify it matches what the callback claims, THEN gate the write' is now stated identically (same order: derive -> compare -> write) for all four listener/callback code paths in this design (SS4.5 text, SS4.5 contact, and now all three SS4.6 callbacks), not just the text listener. No implementation code was introduced -- SS4.6 still contains only the same three bare `export function make...(db) { return async (ctx) => { ... }; }` signature stubs plus the pre-existing regex const declarations (data, not control flow); the 7-step sequence and the gate condition are stated in prose exactly like SS4.5's own existing step list, matching this document's already-passed zero-implementation-code style.

MINOR finding (SS7 AC2 gloss contradicted SS2.2's own table): reworded the AC2 row in SS7 from 'completeness is defined ONLY over the six required columns' to state the same rule SS2.2's derivation table (row 3) and REQ-019-schema.md SS9 already state -- completeness requires all six required columns non-null AND every optional field resolved (non-null or marked skipped) -- with an added clause explaining why skipping doesn't count against completeness (a skip is itself a resolved state, not a missing one). SS2.2 itself was not touched (it was already correct; only the SS7 gloss was wrong).

No other section changed. docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md was not opened for editing (task instruction and my own read of the FAIL confirm it needs no changes -- the gap was entirely in REQ-019.md's SS4.6 handler-sequencing prose, not in the schema DATA-DESIGNER specified).
